## Quick “Ready‑to‑Launch” Checklist (Assuming you already have a working app with Supabase for data and Stripe for payments. 🎉) | Step | What to do | Why it matters | How to do it | |------|------------|----------------|--------------| | **1. Test the Checkout Flow end‑to‑end** | • Sign up → Add card → Complete purchase → Confirmation sent | Ensures no friction for early users & avoids costly refunds. | • Use Stripe test cards.
• Run the flow on a real device or mobile browser.
• Check that the webhook updates the Supabase table and that the next‑screen logic works. | | **2. Verify Environment Variables** | • Make sure `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET`, `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE` are correct for the prod environment. | Accidentally pointing to staging can expose private data. | • In Supabase, double‑check the “API keys” section.
• In Stripe, confirm you’re using the live secret key. | | **3. Audit Security (CORS, Auth, Realtime)** | • Only authenticated users can write to tables.
• Realtime subscriptions don’t leak data. | Prevents data leaks and future legal headaches. | • In Supabase, review the `Auth → Policies` tab for each table.
• Test with a non‑logged‑in session. | | **4. Stripe Dashboard – Live Mode** | • Check that “Live mode” is ON.
• Confirm test mode charges are cleared. | Avoid accidental test charges on live users. | • In Stripe, switch from Test to Live.
• Re‑run a simple “charge” in the dashboard to confirm connectivity. | | **5. Confirm webhooks** | • The webhook URL receives events, updates Supabase, returns 2xx. | Users will notice errors if webhook fails. | • In Stripe → Developers → Webhooks, check the status of the last few events.
• Look in Supabase logs for the record that was updated. | | **6. Handle Payment Failures** | • Show clear error messages (e.g., “Your card was declined”). | Reduces user frustration, ↓ support tickets. | • In your checkout component, catch the error and map Stripe’s status to user‑friendly text. | | **7. Test on Multiple Devices / Browsers** | • iOS, Android, Chrome, Safari, Firefox | Mobile users rarely stick to one browser. | • Use BrowserStack or your own devices. | | **8. Optimize Load Times** | • Images compressed, bundle size < 1 MB, minimal JS | Helps Rank on Product Hunt (fast-first time). | • Run `npm run build` and check output size.
• Use tools like Lighthouse. | | **9. Prepare App Store/Play Store** | • App listing screenshots, app description, privacy policy. | Even if you’re releasing a web‑app, many Product Hunt users browse App Store links. | • Store requirements: enforce HTTPS, handle DEEPLINKS if needed. | | **10. Final sanity‑check on Supabase** | • No open migrations, proper cache, `rls` enabled. | Avoid future dev‑ops nightmares. | • Run `supabase status` or inspect the dashboard. | | **11. Set up Fresh Analytics** | • Google Analytics / Plausible / Mixpanel | Understand where your first users come from. | • Verify first user hits after launch. | | **12. Write a “What’s Happening” Post‑Launch Incident** | • In case of a bug, have a playbook ready. | Production is still production. | • Ready‑to‑copy text for email support or a quick Slack message. | --- ### Quick‑Start “Get‑It‑Ready” Script ```bash # 1️⃣ Verify environment cat .env.production | grep -v '^#' # 2️⃣ Deploy to Supabase supabase deploy --prod # 3️⃣ Deploy to your hosting (Vercel / Netlify) git push main # 4️⃣ Check live webhook curl -I https://api.stripe.com/v1/webhook_endpoints/evt_XXXXX --header "Authorization: Bearer $STRIPE_SECRET" # 5️⃣ Run integration test npx stripe-cli listen ``` --- ## Final Tips Before the Post 1. **Have a backup URL** – In case your main URL is down, link to a static placeholder (a Google Doc “Coming Soon!”). 2. **Make your social media ready** – A short video, GIF, or brain‑pop image of your app. 3. **Draft a FAQ** – Questions like “Do I need a real credit card?” or “Is the app free for 30 days?” 4. **Set a backup for Stripe** – SIY: “If you don’t want to add a card, you can sign up for a $5/month plan via a free trial” – keep the trial logic in place. 5. **Leave the “Hashtag” ready** – #SupabaseStarterKit etc. When you’re ready, hit the **“Show on Product Hunt”** button, fill in the description, attach the images, add the tags, and hit **Submit**. Good luck, you’re all set! 🚀 If you hit any snags, just ping me—happy to run through any last‑minute checks.
